holding_summary: Certiorari review of a Board of Standards and Appeals resolution granting a zoning variance to permit construction of a garage; the resolution's validity could not be attacked by oral statements of board members.
notes: Zoning variance dispute over a garage permit; no bearing on letting or lodging.

holding_summary: Pleading case on whether conducting a real estate and insurance business from part of a dwelling violates a restrictive covenant limiting use to a private dwelling; judgment on the pleadings was improper in a doubtful case.
notes: Restrictive-covenant dispute about a home office/business use, not about letting rooms or lodgers.

holding_summary: Vendor-purchaser dispute over whether an undisclosed restrictive covenant against liquor sales rendered title unmarketable; reformation of the contract was denied.
notes: Title/incumbrance dispute concerning a liquor-sale covenant; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting.

cite: Klepper v. Seymour House Corp. of Ogdensburg, Inc., 246 N.Y. 85
holding_summary: Premises-liability action against a hotel owner and a city for injuries caused by snow and ice falling from a hotel cornice onto a public sidewalk; both defendants were held chargeable with notice and liable in negligence.
notes: Negligence/nuisance case about a hotel building's maintenance duty toward the street; the leasing of stores under the hotel is background only, not a dispute over letting rooms.

holding_summary: Constitutional challenge to the Multiple Dwelling Law under the Home Rule Amendment; the court held the law a valid State health measure not restricted to local 'property, affairs or government of cities.'
notes: Pure Home Rule/constitutional-classification dispute over tenement-house regulation; the opinions do not discuss lodgers, boarders, or short-term letting practices.

holding_summary: Declaratory-judgment action over whether a common grantor was bound to impose a uniform half-acre (or one-acre) minimum-lot-size restriction on unsold parcels of a residential subdivision; no such reciprocal restriction was implied absent disclosure to the buyers.
notes: The deed covenants list 'boarding house' among prohibited uses, but the actual controversy is minimum subdivision-lot acreage; boarding-house use is never litigated.

cite: Millhiser v. Beau Site Co., 251 N.Y. 290
holding_summary: Construing General Business Law section 200, the court held a hotel's $250 statutory limit on liability for guests' safe-deposited valuables applies even where the loss is caused by theft by the hotel's own employee, but the hotel could not invoke the limitation because it failed to post the statute itself alongside its safe-deposit notice.
notes: Concerns an innkeeper's statutory liability limit for guests' valuables, not the legal character or regulation of letting/lodging arrangements.

holding_summary: Dog-bite action turning on whether Gramercy Park, a privately controlled square, was a 'public place' under the Sanitary Code's anti-muzzling ordinance; held it was not, so the ordinance did not apply.
notes: Definition of 'public place' for a dog ordinance; unrelated to letting or lodging.

cite: Varriale v. Brooklyn Edison Co., 252 N.Y. 222
holding_summary: Injunction action over an electric sign's beams spanning the full width of a party wall; held the exclusive appropriation of the wall was a trespass on the co-owner's equal rights of enjoyment.
notes: Party-wall/easement dispute over an advertising sign; unrelated to lodging or letting.

cite: Gray v. Kaufman Dairy & Ice Cream Co., 162 N.Y. 388
holding_summary: Commercial store lease case holding that a landlord's reletting of premises abandoned by a tenant, absent the tenant's assent, effected a surrender by operation of law and released the original tenant from further rent liability.
notes: Commercial storefront lease/surrender dispute; unrelated to residential lodging or boarding.

holding_summary: A tenant in common in possession of land who quarried and sold rock without cotenant consent must account to the cotenants for the value of the rock taken, as waste diminishing the common estate.
notes: Tenancy-in-common/waste accounting dispute over quarried rock; no connection to letting or lodging.

cite: Donnelly v. City of Rochester, 166 N.Y. 315
holding_summary: Wrongful-death action against a city for an inadequately guarded areaway on a sidewalk; the sufficiency of the guard rail was a jury question, and the city was chargeable with notice of the long-standing danger.
notes: Municipal sidewalk-negligence case; unrelated to lodging or letting.

cite: People ex rel. Pumpyansky v. Keating, 168 N.Y. 390
holding_summary: Mandamus proceeding over the city's authority to license newspaper stands built under elevated-railroad stairways; the writ was denied because the record did not establish a clear right to full removal of the stand.
notes: Street-encroachment licensing dispute over news stands; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

cite: Bly v. Edison Electric Illuminating Co., 172 N.Y. 1
holding_summary: The Court of Appeals held that a tenant in possession under a lease made during the existence of a nuisance may nonetheless maintain an action to abate it and recover her own damages, rejecting the rule (drawn from elevated-railroad cases) that only the landlord who leased before the nuisance arose could sue. The plaintiff's business of keeping a boarding house and renting rooms to lodgers was treated as an ordinary possessory interest whose diminished rental income was a compensable, legally protected loss distinct from any injury to the landlord's reversion.

quotes.text: In order to determine the question of law presented by this appeal, it becomes necessary to understand more fully the situation of the parties. In the year 1888 the plaintiff rented the premises known as No. 33 West 26th street, Hew York city, until the first of May, 1890, and occupied the same as tenant keeping a boarding house.
That the aforesaid acts have prevented the plaintiff from renting the rooms of her house, have injured her furniture and household effects and have caused her an expense for laundry work.

notes: Core holding is about tenant standing to sue for nuisance, not the legality of boarding-house letting itself; the boarding-house/lodger facts are background but the court treats that rental income as an ordinary, legally protected business interest of the tenant-operator, which is why it is coded favorable rather than irrelevant.

cite: Cudlip v. New York Evening Journal Publishing Co., 174 N.Y. 158
holding_summary: Libel action reversed for improper admission of an ex parte affidavit exonerating the plaintiff of a theft charge; the affidavit's prejudicial effect on damages required a new trial.
notes: A boarding house (kept by a Mrs. Morgan, where the plaintiff had boarded) is mentioned only in passing as background to a libel/evidence dispute over a stolen ring; not relevant under the passing-mention exclusion.

cite: People ex rel. Lieberman v. Vandecarr, 175 N.Y. 440
holding_summary: Habeas corpus challenge to a Sanitary Code section requiring a Board of Health permit to sell milk; the permit requirement was upheld as a reasonable exercise of the police power.
notes: Public-health licensing case about milk sales; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

holding_summary: Upheld, as a valid police-power health measure, the Labor Law provision limiting bakery employees to sixty hours per week / ten hours per day.
notes: Bakery labor-hours regulation case; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting of dwellings.

holding_summary: A three-story building interiorly divided so each floor could house a separate family violated a restrictive covenant against tenement houses and requiring private dwellings only; the remedy was an injunction against tenement-house use rather than demolition.
notes: Concerns a private covenant against permanent multi-family (tenement) division of a residence, not compensated short-term letting of rooms to lodgers or boarders.
